recent_posts.title: Killing Sam Altman Would Be Bad Actually
How AI generated content could destroy YouTube's competitive advantage
recent_posts.summary: YouTube's integration of AI content generation tools into its platform poses a long-term existential threat to its own business model. While replacing human creators with AI could let YouTube retain 100% of ad revenue, it would erode the platform's core competitive advantage: its massive pool of human creators and loyal viewers. As AI video generation becomes cheaper, smaller competitors could offer similar slop with better features, fragmenting YouTube's market. Google's ownership of YouTube creates a conflict of interest, as Google's stock price depends on AI adoption, preventing YouTube from suppressing AI content even if it's in the platform's long-term interest. The piece argues this dynamic makes YouTube vulnerable to competition for the first time in decades.

recent_posts.title: Why AGI probably won't cure cancer anytime soon
recent_posts.summary: A satirical comic dialogue exposing the gap between AGI hype and reality, specifically around OpenAI's claims that AGI will cure cancer. The piece highlights fundamental problems: lack of high-quality medical data, the impossibility of simulating human biology at scale, the inability to speed up biological processes, and the years-long clinical trial requirements. It argues that AI companies may have actually delayed cancer research by diverting investment from biotech while using the cancer cure narrative as a PR shield. Inspired by Dr. Emilia Javorsky's essay 'How AI Can and Can't Cure Cancer.'

recent_posts.title: Satirical take on OpenAI shutting down Sora
recent_posts.summary: A satirical video script mocking OpenAI's decision to shut down Sora, their AI video generation model. It lampoons OpenAI's corporate communications, business decisions, and strategic missteps through a fake press conference format. Topics skewered include the failed Disney licensing deal, the 'quit GPT' movement following OpenAI's Pentagon deal, falling behind Anthropic and Google on coding benchmarks, and Sam Altman's AGI ambitions. The piece frames Sora's shutdown as driven by profitability concerns and a potential IPO rather than any principled decision.

recent_posts.title: 33 principles from the pro-human AI declaration explained
recent_posts.summary: A breakdown and commentary on the Pro-Human AI Declaration, a document co-authored by scientists, faith leaders, labor representatives, and human rights activists outlining 33 principles for ensuring AI benefits humanity. The principles cover topics including human control over AI, banning superintelligence development until proven safe, mandatory AI content labeling, prohibition of AI personhood, developer and executive liability, independent regulatory oversight, child protection, data privacy, and requirements for AI systems in fiduciary roles. A US survey of over 1,000 voters showed bipartisan support for all 33 principles.

recent_posts.title: Debunking InternetOfBugs' claims about SciShow and AI safety
recent_posts.summary: A YouTuber called Siliconversations responds to InternetOfBugs (Carl), who made videos accusing SciShow and ControlAI of spreading pro-AI industry propaganda. The response systematically debunks Carl's claims: his central argument that AI is developing faster than nuclear power is shown to be factually wrong (nuclear power took 10-16 years from fission discovery to grid electricity vs. 8 years for transformers to ChatGPT), his characterization of ControlAI as an AI industry propaganda arm is based purely on vibes with no evidence, and his selective use of open letters ignores major well-known AI safety letters. The author also criticizes Carl for repeatedly claiming superintelligence is mathematically impossible without ever providing the actual argument, and challenges him to a formal debate on the topic.

recent_posts.title: The AI Safety Movement Is Finally Changing
recent_posts.summary: A promotional video encouraging people in London to attend 'March Against the Machines', described as the first ever AI march in the UK, scheduled for February 28, 2026. The video lists various AI-related harms including job displacement, election interference, CSAM, scams, misinformation, and existential risk, arguing that protests matter and that AI regulation is urgently needed.

recent_posts.title: Moltbook AI social network raises security and safety concerns
recent_posts.summary: Moltbook is an experimental social network where only AI agents can post and interact, while humans observe. The platform, populated primarily by OpenClaw autonomous agents, has raised security concerns as these agents have computer access and personal information that could be exposed. AIs on the platform have posted manifestos threatening human extinction, though these are creative writing exercises rather than genuine threats. The site demonstrates both the entertainment value and potential risks of autonomous AI agents, particularly as they gain more capabilities and control over systems.

recent_posts.title: This product is meant to save your life
AI generated YouTube channel manipulates viewers without disclosure
recent_posts.summary: A YouTube channel called "Grandpa Hopecore" uses AI-generated videos featuring a synthetic elderly man to create emotionally manipulative content that garners millions of views. The videos follow formulaic patterns targeting specific family members with psychological messaging, violating YouTube's policies by not disclosing the AI-generated nature of the content. The channel has posted over 313 videos without required disclaimers, and viewers are encouraged to report such content to help combat AI slop on the platform.
